pr_title: LE Audio: Read PACS location as unicast client
pr_body:
The unicast client will now read the unicast server's PACS location values.

This required adding a way of exposing the value, by adding a unicast_client_cb structure.

This also subscribes to the location characteristic (if supported by the remote server). 

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/46763

issue_context.title: LE Audio: Unicast Audio read PAC location
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The BAP unicast client should read the PAC location, if available, on the unicast server. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We are already reading context as part of the discovery procedure; consider doing the same for location. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
It can also be read explicitly using a new function. 

**Additional context**
The location value shall also be exposed to the application.

review_comments:
Are you going to make use of the locations somewhere in the stack?
Maybe it's not needed to discover and read locations if user did not registered `unicast_client_cbs->location` callback?

> Maybe it's not needed to discover and read locations if user did not registered `unicast_client_cbs->location` callback?

Hmm, yeah I guess that if the location callback wasn't set, we could skip it (that is seemingly OK with the spec). In mos cases the callback structure will be constant and not changing, but there's technically nothing stopping the application from registering the callbacks with `unicast_client_cbs->location = NULL`, and then later assign a callback to it, but that is kind of a weird use case. 

Since this is a once-per-connection type of deal, I think it's OK to discover and subscribe to locations, regardless of the callback.
If there is no location, then that means that there is a single stream, right?

Hmm, I can't find anything in PACS or BAP that says that. 

What we have in BAP is:
> Support of multiplexing of Audio Channels for a Sink ASE is determined by exposing a value of the Supported_Audio_Channel_Counts (see Section 4.3.1) LTV structure greater than 1 in any Sink PAC [5] characteristic.
> - If multiplexing of Audio Channels is not supported, the number of Sink ASEs shall be equal to or greater than the number of bits set to 0b1 in the Sink Audio Locations characteristic value.
> - If multiplexing of Audio Channels is supported, the number of Sink ASEs shall be equal to or greater than the number of bits set to 0b1 in the Sink Audio Locations characteristic value divided by the highest number of Audio Channels supported in the Supported_Audio_Channel_Counts LTV.

To me it doesn't seem to require that location has to be there for multiplexing, nor does it prohibit the location value when multiplexing is not support (at least from the adopted BAP spec). So the location characteristic seems to be completely optional.
@Thalley I think there is a requirement for the location information to be able to set Audio_Channel_Allocation when configuring the ASE for LC3.(mentioned in BAP chap 4

Correct, Table 4.1 has
> If Min Sink Audio Locations per server > 1, Sink Audio Locations shall exist and shall support > 1 location by setting > 1 bits to 0b1 in the characteristic value

And the table does not have a configuration where a unicast server may have multiple Sink ASEs without having multiple locations, and thus have the PACS sink audio location characteristic. 

So a unicast server cannot have a LEFT sink ASE and a RIGHT sink ASE without having the sink audio characteristic with a least 2 bits set. 
Curiously this also prohibits a unicast server to have e.g. 2 LEFT sink ASEs, as that would not satisfy the requirement of setting more than 1 bit in the location. 

These requirement is for LC3 only though, right? So for another codec wouldn't it still be legal to have 2 sink ASEs without the location characteristic? 

Keep in mind that these are also _configurations_, and not _capabilities_, so it's a requirement that needs to be satisfied at runtime, right?

I think the implementation should continue to function even without the characteristic - to be able to handle non LC3 cases.
But I don't see why you could not have two ASEs configured to the same location (for example LEFT) - the content might be of different type - instructional vs media - and you want to do local mixing that depends on the application (A car might only want to render the instructions on the left front speaker).
But yes you cannot configure a single ASE to have two channels to be rendered at the same output.
If you really need to make something that can do this you could make your device available for different variants of Left (for example left back) - and then locally rout them to the same output.

Right - My point was that there isn't an audio configuration for LC3 where a device may have 2 sink ASEs and a single location supported (e.g. LEFT), but as you mentioned a device could simply just write FRONT_LEFT and SIDE_LEFT or something. 

> But yes you cannot configure a single ASE to have two channels to be rendered at the same output.

Is that also a restriction? e.g. in the case of a simple car where you probably have a left and right speaker (i.e. 2 locations), can you not have 2 media CIS (to each speaker (LEFT and RIGHT)), and a 3rd CIS only going to the left?

An ASE (audio stream endpoint) is linked to a only one CIS - either C_to_P or P_to_C. That CIS can carry multiple channels - and the PAC specifies how many channels a device can support for a single ASE ( for example 2 for Left/Right on same CIS), whereas the locations specify where each of these can be routed.
When configuring an ASE you specify the location to use by the channel allocation (and not the channel count) where each bit represents a channel in the stream for that particular ASE (linked to one direction on a CIS) - Again as you mention this is only specified for LC3, but using generic assigned numbers that could be applied to any codec.
This also means that there is no way for a client to specify that a stream (ASE) carries two channels to be rendered on the same location (speaker) - as a channel allocation with only one bit set means that the stream carries only one channel.

> Right - My point was that there isn't an audio configuration for LC3 where a device may have 2 sink ASEs and a single location supported (e.g. LEFT), but as you mentioned a device could simply just write FRONT_LEFT and SIDE_LEFT or something.

Actually there is. You can have multiple ASES and only a single location - for example this is how our earbuds work. They have one location, but will accept up to two streams (ASEs) for that single location. Selection of stream and/or mixing will be done locally. To use this you create two CIS'es and configure the channel allocation for each ASE to be the same.

> Is that also a restriction? e.g. in the case of a simple car where you probably have a left and right speaker (i.e. 2 locations), can you not have 2 media CIS (to each speaker (LEFT and RIGHT)), and a 3rd CIS only going to the left?

Yes you can have this configuration if the device exposes 3 ASEs. You could even stuff both left and right channels into the same CIS and thereby have the setup using only two ASEs.

> Actually there is. You can have multiple ASES and only a single location - for example this is how our earbuds work. They have one location, but will accept up to two streams (ASEs) for that single location. Selection of stream and/or mixing will be done locally. To use this you create two CIS'es and configure the channel allocation for each ASE to be the same.

Sorry, wasn't clear: There isn't a BAP spec defined configuration for a single server having 2 ASEs and a single location: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2520413/176679263-8bc1bfad-3d99-4cfd-98b8-6caf09235660.png)

> This also means that there is no way for a client to specify that a stream (ASE) carries two channels to be rendered on the same location (speaker) - as a channel allocation with only one bit set means that the stream carries only one channel.

Correct (for LC3 and other single-channel codecs) :)
